import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load original file
orig_file = r"C:\Users\sandeeppawar\Downloads\aida-eval\runs\aida-ctrl\work\FG_151\Young_Pioneers_counselor_political_quality-1.csv"
orig_df = pd.read_csv(orig_file)

print(f"Original file shape: {orig_df.shape}")
print(f"Original columns: {list(orig_df.columns)}")

# Get numeric columns
numeric_cols = orig_df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns.tolist()
non_numeric_cols = orig_df.select_dtypes(exclude=[np.number]).columns.tolist()

print(f"\nNumeric columns: {len(numeric_cols)}")
print(f"Non-numeric columns: {len(non_numeric_cols)}")
print(f"Non-numeric: {non_numeric_cols}")

# Compute correlation matrix
print("\nComputing pairwise correlations...")
corr_matrix = orig_df[numeric_cols].corr()

# Implement the algorithm: drop columns with higher embedded numbers when |corr| > 0.9
columns_to_drop = set()

# Find all pairs with |correlation| > 0.9
high_corr_pairs = []
for i in range(len(numeric_cols)):
    for j in range(i+1, len(numeric_cols)):
        corr_val = corr_matrix.iloc[i, j]
        if abs(corr_val) > 0.9:
            col1 = numeric_cols[i]
            col2 = numeric_cols[j]
            # Extract embedded numbers
            num1 = int(''.join(filter(str.isdigit, col1)))
            num2 = int(''.join(filter(str.isdigit, col2)))
            high_corr_pairs.append((col1, col2, corr_val, num1, num2))

print(f"Found {len(high_corr_pairs)} pairs with |correlation| > 0.9")

# Now iteratively drop columns
remaining_cols = set(numeric_cols)

iteration = 0
while True:
    iteration += 1
    # Recompute correlations on remaining columns
    remaining_list = sorted(list(remaining_cols))
    if len(remaining_list) < 2:
        break
    
    corr_sub = orig_df[remaining_list].corr()
    
    # Find any pair with |corr| > 0.9
    found_high_corr = False
    for i in range(len(remaining_list)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(remaining_list)):
            corr_val = corr_sub.iloc[i, j]
            if abs(corr_val) > 0.9:
                col1 = remaining_list[i]
                col2 = remaining_list[j]
                num1 = int(''.join(filter(str.isdigit, col1)))
                num2 = int(''.join(filter(str.isdigit, col2)))
                
                # Drop the one with larger number
                to_drop = col2 if num2 > num1 else col1
                remaining_cols.discard(to_drop)
                columns_to_drop.add(to_drop)
                found_high_corr = True
                print(f"Iteration {iteration}: {col1} <-> {col2} (corr={corr_val:.4f}) -> drop {to_drop}")
                break
        if found_high_corr:
            break
    
    if not found_high_corr:
        break

# Compute correlation matrix
print("\nComputing correlations...")
corr_matrix = orig_numeric.corr()

# Algorithm: iteratively drop columns with higher embedded number when |corr| > 0.9
remaining_cols = set(orig_numeric.columns)
dropped_cols = []

iteration = 0
max_iterations = 1000

while iteration < max_iterations:
    iteration += 1
    remaining_list = sorted(list(remaining_cols))
    
    if len(remaining_list) < 2:
        break
    
    # Recompute correlation on remaining columns
    corr_sub = orig_numeric[remaining_list].corr()
    
    # Find first pair with |corr| > 0.9
    found_high_corr = False
    for i in range(len(remaining_list)):
        if found_high_corr:
            break
        for j in range(i+1, len(remaining_list)):
            corr_val = corr_sub.iloc[i, j]
            if abs(corr_val) > 0.9:
                col1 = remaining_list[i]
                col2 = remaining_list[j]
                
                # Extract embedded numbers
                num1 = int(''.join(filter(str.isdigit, col1)))
                num2 = int(''.join(filter(str.isdigit, col2)))
                
                # Drop the one with larger number
                to_drop = col2 if num2 > num1 else col1
                remaining_cols.discard(to_drop)
                dropped_cols.append(to_drop)
                
                if iteration <= 15:  # Print first 15
                    print(f"Iter {iteration}: {col1} <-> {col2} (corr={corr_val:.4f}) -> drop {to_drop}")
                
                found_high_corr = True
                break
    
    if not found_high_corr:
        print(f"\nNo more pairs with |corr| > 0.9 found after {iteration-1} iterations")
        break
